atoms.canonical_statement: The CheckMate 067 long-term follow-up report evaluated 6.5-year efficacy and safety of nivolumab plus ipilimumab and nivolumab alone versus ipilimumab in advanced melanoma, including a first report of melanoma-specific survival.

Eligible participants were adults with previously untreated, unresectable or metastatic histologically confirmed stage III or IV melanoma, known BRAF V600 mutation status, and ECOG performance status 0 or 1.

population.label: Eligible adults with untreated unresectable or metastatic stage III/IV melanoma

atoms.canonical_statement: Of 1,296 patients enrolled, 945 were randomly assigned: 314 to nivolumab plus ipilimumab, 316 to nivolumab, and 315 to ipilimumab.
The combination arm received nivolumab 1 mg/kg plus ipilimumab 3 mg/kg every 3 weeks for four doses, followed by nivolumab 3 mg/kg every 2 weeks.

exposures.details: Nivolumab 1 mg/kg plus ipilimumab 3 mg/kg every 3 weeks for four doses, followed by nivolumab 3 mg/kg every 2 weeks

exposures.details: Nivolumab 3 mg/kg every 2 weeks

atoms.canonical_statement: The ipilimumab arm received ipilimumab 3 mg/kg every 3 weeks for four doses.

exposures.details: Ipilimumab 3 mg/kg every 3 weeks for four doses

atoms.canonical_statement: Patients were randomly assigned 1:1:1, with stratification by BRAF mutation status, AJCC seventh-edition metastasis stage, and tumor PD-L1 status.

Treatment regimens were placebo-matched for blinding, and treatment stopped for progressive disease, unacceptable toxicity, or consent withdrawal, with investigator-permitted treatment beyond progression when clinical benefit persisted without substantial adverse events.
Progression-free survival was investigator assessed and was a coprimary endpoint for each nivolumab-containing group versus ipilimumab.
Overall survival was a coprimary endpoint for each nivolumab-containing group versus ipilimumab.
Objective response rate was a secondary endpoint assessed by investigators.
Melanoma-specific survival was a descriptive post hoc endpoint in which melanoma deaths were events and deaths from other causes were censored.

outcome.definition: Death due to melanoma; nonmelanoma deaths censored

atoms.canonical_statement: Treatment-free interval was the time from the last study-drug dose to initiation of subsequent systemic therapy or the last known date alive, excluding specified patients who died or left follow-up before subsequent therapy.
Efficacy endpoints were analyzed in the intent-to-treat population. Updated P values for the 6.5-year PFS, OS, and ORR assessments were descriptive.
The trial was not designed or powered for a formal comparison of nivolumab plus ipilimumab versus nivolumab monotherapy.
Median PFS was 11.5 months in the nivolumab plus ipilimumab arm, with 95% CI 8.7 to 19.3 months.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors concluded that 6.5-year CheckMate 067 follow-up showed durable improved outcomes with nivolumab plus ipilimumab or nivolumab versus ipilimumab, with descriptive analyses favoring the combination over nivolumab monotherapy.

The study report states support from Bristol Myers Squibb, NCI grant P30CA008748 to Jedd D. Wolchok, and a grant to James Larkin from the National Institute for Health Research Royal Marsden-Institute of Cancer Research Biomedical Research Centre.
The disclosure pages report multiple financial relationships with oncology companies. Tuba Bas and Corey Ritchings were employed by Bristol Myers Squibb, the study sponsor.
